As someone who only played Pokemon Yellow and Gold, back in the day, I was thinking of getting Sun for my cousin for Christmas. Your post makes me reconsider this. Despite the flaws, would you still recommend the game for a kid today or is it too disappointing?

With my post I was mostly trying to say "look everything is in line for this company, why can't they put together a really great game". Nevertheless, I'm still enjoying the game. Yea I'd recommend it, because despite its flaws, its still a good game. Aside from the hand holding, none of the things I listed break the game.

What I liked about the game:

  • The Alolan Forms were a nice twist on classic Pokemon for the most part. Gave quite a few species that needed it a nice boost.

  • Z Moves are interesting and constantly kept me curious what the next one would be.

  • No more fucking Gyms was a wonderful change of pace.

  • Riding Pokemon was a nice way to eliminate HMs and some items, and riding Stoutland everywhere was fun.

  • Actually interesting story, especially compared to how uninteresting Gen 6's was to me.

  • The Pelago and Pokemon Refresh was a surprisingly fun distraction and a nice way to implement some optional boosts and good berry growing mechanics.

  • EXP Share made the times I had to grind go by a lot faster and could be cut off most of the time.

  • The Ultra Beasts and related events remind me a bit of Earthbound.

  • Side quests, even if most of them boil down to "get money for catching specific Pokemon."

  • Leech Life buff is an awesome new tool for Pokemon that can learn it. Other various buffs/nerfs that were needed too (Dark Void having its accuracy cut further)

  • Totem Pokemon made for nice bosses, and I liked the call for help mechanic during these battles. The Totem plus a teamate was more challenging than most Gyms to me.

  • Elite Four members having 5 Pokemon each again.

Cons:

  • Questionable usefulness of some Alolan forms (Dugtrio having a cool ability the requires contact).

  • Walls of tutorial text on the first island, often having basic points repeated 2-3 times (Main characters, trainers, and trainer tips signs)

  • The stat judge having to have a side quest to complete is annoying.

  • Low exp from wild Pokemon, makes grinding annoying when there aren't any more trainers to beat.

  • The removal of Super Training, even if it did get replaced by new options.

  • Very poor performance (on the original 3DS hardware anyway) that necessitated removing triple/rotation battles
